justification_text:
The point estimates for each time horizon—1 day, 1 week, and 1 month—are all the same because they represent the central "best guess" for the forecasted value at each of those time intervals, based on the information available at the time of the forecast. The underlying assumption here is that the base case conditions (e.g., market trends, economic indicators, or other relevant data sources) suggest stability or no significant directional change over the forecasted period. While short-term fluctuations are possible, the expectation is that, on average, the outcome will center around this value of 255.78.

The width of the confidence intervals reflects the increasing uncertainty as the forecast horizon lengthens. Over a single day, there isn't much time for unpredictable events to cause large swings, so the 90% confidence interval is relatively narrow (252.08 to 259.48). By the 1-week horizon, uncertainty grows, as more factors—like market volatility, external news events, or behavioral changes—could start to influence the outcome. This is why the range widens to 247.11 to 264.45. Over a month, the uncertainty is even greater, resulting in a much broader range (238.45 to 273.11), because there is more time for complex interactions between variables to compound, or for unforeseen events to occur.

There are specific risks or events that could push outcomes outside of the stated intervals, especially at the longer time horizons. Examples might include unexpected geopolitical crises, major policy changes, or significant shifts in underlying economic conditions—any of which could create sudden and extreme deviations from the forecast. Additionally, rare or "black swan" events, such as catastrophic natural disasters, system outages, or unprecedented market behavior, could drive outcomes far beyond these calculated bounds. While the confidence intervals aim to account for most conceivable scenarios, forecasting inherently involves some blind spots, especially when rare events or non-linear dynamics come into play.
